problem.statement: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.

nums.meaning: The sequence of values to inspect.

box.meaning: The set of values encountered before the current num.

num.meaning: The value currently being inspected from nums.

representation_requirements.description: Represent nums in processing order and identify the current position.
Represent box as the distinct values encountered before the current num.
Represent checking whether num is in box before adding a new num.
Represent immediate true termination on a duplicate and false termination after exhaustion.

semantic_invariants.statement: A duplicate exists exactly when some value appears at least twice in nums.
Before processing the current num, box contains exactly the distinct values processed earlier in nums.
num is a duplicate exactly when num is already in box.
A non-duplicate num is added to box only after its membership has been checked.
The result is true if a duplicate is detected and false only after nums is exhausted without one.

completion_evidence.description: The learner identifies that any value appearing at least twice satisfies the condition.
The learner tracks how box represents previously processed values.
The learner states or applies the membership check before adding num.
The learner distinguishes duplicate-found termination from exhaustion without a duplicate.

terminal_behavior: Terminate and return true immediately when num is already in box.
Add num to box and continue when num is not already in box.
After all values are processed without a duplicate, return false.

problem.statement: Reverse a singly linked list and return the new head.

prev.meaning: The head of the already reversed prefix; null before the first reversal and the new list head at termination.

curr.meaning: The first node in the remaining portion of the original list whose link has not yet been reversed.

next_node.meaning: The original successor of curr saved before curr's link is changed.

representation_requirements.description: Represent curr as the first unprocessed node in the remaining original chain.
Represent next_node as the original successor of curr before curr's link changes.
Represent the processed prefix with each processed node pointing toward prev.
Represent processed nodes in the reversed prefix and unprocessed nodes in the remaining suffix.

semantic_invariants.statement: curr is either null or the first node not yet rewired in original traversal order.
next_node equals curr's original successor before curr's link is changed.
prev is the head of a prefix containing exactly the processed nodes, with links reversed relative to their original order.
When curr is null, all input nodes are contained in prev and prev is the new head.

completion_evidence.description: The response identifies curr as the next unprocessed node.
The response preserves curr's original successor in next_node before rewiring.
The response maps the current node's next link to prev while retaining the saved successor.
The response advances until curr is null and returns prev as the new head.

terminal_behavior: For an empty input list, return the empty-list head.
While curr is not null, save curr's original successor in next_node before changing curr's link.
Set curr's next link to prev, then advance prev to curr and curr to next_node.
When curr is null, return prev as the new head.

problem.statement: Count connected groups of 1s in a 2D grid using 4-direction adjacency.

grid.meaning: The 2D binary grid whose connected groups of 1s are counted.

r.meaning: The current row position in grid.

c.meaning: The current column position in grid.

count.meaning: The number of connected groups discovered so far.

stack.meaning: A last-in-first-out collection of cells pending exploration within the current component.

representation_requirements.description: Represent each cell with its valid up, down, left, and right neighbors; diagonal adjacency is excluded.
Represent count as a counter initialized to zero and incremented once for each newly discovered component.
Represent traversal over every valid row and column position so no component start is skipped.
Mark a discovered land cell as visited, such as by changing its grid value from 1 to 0, before adding it to the frontier.
Represent the current component's pending cells in stack and process them using depth-first traversal.

semantic_invariants.statement: Two cells belong to the same component only when connected through a path of horizontally or vertically adjacent 1s.
count increases exactly when the scan encounters an unvisited cell containing 1.
Every cell added to stack belongs to the current component and is marked visited before it can be added again.
When stack becomes empty, every cell reachable from the component's starting cell through four-direction adjacency has been visited.
After all valid grid positions have been scanned and all discovered components explored, count equals the number of connected groups of 1s.

completion_evidence.description: The learner identifies the grid cells and the four allowed adjacency directions.
The learner states the condition that distinguishes an unvisited 1 from water or an already visited cell.
The learner describes marking a discovered cell, pushing it onto stack, and exploring its valid four-direction neighbors until the stack is empty.
The learner identifies count after the complete grid traversal as the number of connected groups.

terminal_behavior: Initialize count to zero and scan every valid cell in grid.
For each unvisited 1, increment count and explore its full four-direction component using stack.
Terminate after every grid position has been scanned and every discovered component has been fully explored.

problem.statement: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.

nums.meaning: The input collection of numeric values to scan.

k.meaning: The positive rank and maximum number of values retained in heap.

heap.meaning: The min-heap containing the largest up to k values seen so far.

num.meaning: The value currently processed from nums.

representation_requirements.description: Represent nums as an ordered sequence whose values are processed one at a time.
Represent heap as a min-heap with its smallest retained value at the root and capacity k.
Compare num with the heap root to decide whether num belongs in the retained top-k set.

semantic_invariants.statement: The target is the value whose rank among the input values is k when values are ordered from largest to smallest.
When heap contains k retained values, its root is the smallest value currently retained.
The heap contains no more than k values.
After processing any prefix of nums, heap contains the largest up to k values from that prefix.
Each insertion or root replacement followed by heap restoration preserves the top-k-prefix invariant.
After all valid input values are processed, the heap root is the kth largest value.

completion_evidence.description: States the target rank and relates k to the desired largest-value position.
Explains that the min-heap root is the smallest value among retained candidates.
States that the bounded heap retains the largest up to k values seen so far.
Describes inserting until capacity k and replacing the root when a later value exceeds it, followed by heap restoration.
Identifies the final heap root as the kth largest value after the scan.

terminal_behavior: Process each value in nums in order while maintaining the bounded min-heap.
After nums is exhausted, return heap[0] as the kth largest value for valid input with 1 <= k <= len(nums).
